purpose: Exact new primary-source applications for final P18 acceptance; no universal non-Kahler claim

primary_applications.application: Theorems 1.6, 1.10, 12.2 and 13.2; complete printed global algorithm and compact-space gluing proof read. Compact reduced analytic main graph has a proper smooth resolution preserving its smooth locus. Source ideal principalization is finite. Smooth-source blowups preserve a generic divisor: a divisorial center gives an isomorphism and a center of codimension at least two misses the generic point. The cold construction uses source principalization followed by the explicit finite target extraction, independently of the author's target-resolution route.

Entire Theorem 2.13 and printed proofs of Proposition 2.14, Corollary 2.16, Propositions 2.18 and 2.20 read. Theorem 2.13 explicitly imports BFJ Theorem A, rather than giving its proof; this is an imported foundation. Point-Lelong profiles on all smooth projective modifications are obtained from generic divisor profiles by further point blowups in base dimension at least two. The closed-base all-real-weight criterion is applied in a common sufficiently large closed background. No criterion on a general non-Kahler target is imported.

Whole Theorems 1.6, 1.7, Lemma 1.10 and Corollary 1.12 with their complete printed proofs/sketches read. Exact convention conversion: the source uses exp(-2m phi) and (2m)^(-1) log sum|g|^2. Apply it to phi=U/2, then double the approximating potentials to obtain m^(-1) log I(mU). Curvature errors also double and still vanish. Thus the translated statement in final premise 12 matches the article's exp(-tU) convention; it is not a verbatim quotation. Dyadic indices are unchanged and all positive weights are rescaled consistently.

The source definition exp(-phi), Theorem 1.1, and the entire printed dimension-one and induction proof in Section 3 read. On a sufficiently small polydisk a smooth correction makes tU psh and negative. Its bounded factor does not change integrability or the strict increase to a weight t-prime>t. Ohsawa-Takegoshi and the source curve-selection lemma remain imported foundations.

Entire Theorem 2.6(i),(ii) and printed proof read. Tensor product Hilbert bases and diagonal restriction give the local subadditivity used for dyadic analytic representatives. Smooth quasi-psh corrections change integrability only by bounded factors. Positive rescaling translates the source convention to exp(-tU). Diagonal restriction and its supporting foundations are imported, not recursively certified.

Entire Corollary II.8.6, proper-mapping Theorem II.8.8 and their simultaneous printed Remmert-Stein proof read, including compact analytic main graphs. Entire IX.1.1-1.5 Nakayama, Artin-Rees, Krull and closed-module proofs read: intersection_k(J+m^k)=J justifies the coherent submersion ideal identity from every Taylor coefficient. Standard foundations inside these proofs remain imported.
